submitted.rationale: Index 28 (Sb 0.67) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0035%. XRD at indices 14, 23 and 28 shows the same cubic fluorite-like phase along the whole line. MEGNet predicts that Sb-rich mixed-valence oxides have gaps well below the 3.2 eV photon energy (Sb2O4 1.67 eV, Sb6O13 2.05 eV), while the Y2O3 host is at 5.57 eV, which fits EQE rising with Sb content. Index 28 is the most Sb-rich composition in the library.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE was about 0 (-0.00014%) despite the favourable YSbO4 prediction (on hull, 2.97 eV gap). The XRD did not match YSbO4.
Measured EQE 0.0008%, below index 28. The wide-gap Y2O3-like host limits absorption.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts YSbO4 on the hull, and MEGNet-HSE gives it a 2.97 eV gap, below the 3.2 eV photon energy, so it can absorb. Y3SbO7 (3.6 eV) and Y2O3 are too wide to absorb, so the Y-rich side looks weak. Index 23 (Sb 0.52) is the closest candidate to the SbY stoichiometry. XRD at 23 shows a cubic fluorite-like pattern that does not match the MP phases well, so the phase assignment is uncertain.

Moderate support: MEGNet gives the Sb-rich mixed-valence oxides narrow gaps (Sb2O4 1.67 eV, Sb6O13 2.05 eV), so pushing toward Sb should improve visible absorption at 3.2 eV. Index 23 gave near-zero EQE. XRD shows the same cubic phase along the whole line, so composition-driven changes in electronic structure are the main lever. Index 28 is the most Sb-rich candidate available.

Against on physics, but useful for exploration: MEGNet puts the Y2O3 host gap at 5.57 eV, far above the 3.2 eV photons, so intrinsic absorption at the Y-rich end should be negligible. Only dilute-Sb defect-state absorption could help there. The measured trend (23 about 0, 28 at 0.0035%) favors Sb-rich compositions, but 28 is already the library edge, and points between 23 and 28 are unlikely to beat it. The Y-rich end is the only unexplored region with meaningful GP uncertainty, so I'm spending the last measurement there as a hedge.
